findings.title: Approved C# bytes are not revalidated after acquiring their prelaunch read locks
sourceCitations: SOURCE-BODY-013, Invoke-E04AProfileProof.ps1, physical lines 1517-1527: Rules-SourceFiles hashes and compares source/stage files before lock acquisition.

SOURCE-BODY-013, physical lines 1551-1562: Prepare-RulesChallenge subsequently opens read locks, records a fresh topology and publishes the challenge without checking the held bytes against the approved descriptors.

findings.analysis: A staged target file can change after Rules-SourceFiles hashes version A but before File.Open acquires its lock. The lock then holds version B. Rules-Topology records B without comparing that snapshot to the approved descriptors, and the direct UBT root can start. The later producer check may refuse the mismatch, but it occurs after the changed target source can be compiled and its constructor executed. This is a prelaunch validation gap, independent of the expressly unclaimed continuous directory monitoring.
findings.requiredRemediation: After acquiring each source lock, validate the approved length and SHA256 using the held stream, and validate the final prelaunch source/topology snapshot against the frozen approved membership before Invoke-Root. Add a controlled fixture covering mutation between the earlier hash and lock acquisition, requiring refusal before launch. Refreeze and obtain affected fresh review.
